 On The 31st Of March, 2026
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 13520 of 2026
 Suresh Jatav
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Devendra Kumar Sharma - Advocate for the applicant
 Mrs. Kalpana Parmar - Pp for the State.
 Shri Abhishek Tiwari- Advocate for the complainant.

Order 
The applicant has filed this First bail application under Section 482 of BNSS/438 of Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail.
Applicant apprehends his arrest in connection with Crime No.60/2025 registered at Police Station Cantt District Guna (M.P.) in relation to the offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC.

According to the prosecution story, on 19.01.2025, the complainant Ramgopal Sahu, son of Mathuralal Sahu, resident of Sakatpur Road, submitted a written application at Police Station Cantt,
stating that he is a resident of Sakatpur, District Guna, and that he had purchased a piece of land bearing Survey No. 189/8, Min, Patwari Halka No. 62, New No. 05, Panchayat Sakatpur,
Development Block Guna, Tehsil and District Guna, having an area of 0.2020 hectare, measuring 75.5  40, with a total area of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10604 2 MCRC-13520-2026 2,235 square feet (i.e., 207.71 square meters), which had been sold to him through a registered sale deed dated 03.05.2024 by the accused persons after receiving the entire sale consideration amount of Rs.6,85,000/- in the presence of two witnesses, namely Ramkrishna Yadav and Arvind Soni, prior to the execution of the registered sale deed.

However, it is alleged that the accused persons Suresh Jatav ( present applicant), Raju Kadam son of Ramesh Chandra Kadam,
and Mahendra Kushwah son of Devilal Kushwah, acting in criminal conspiracy and with fraudulent intention, subsequently prepared forged documents and again sold the same land which had already been sold to the complainant--to Durjendra Kushwah son of Gajanand Kushwah on 16.05.2024 and 17.05.2024, by means of fabrication and manipulation of documents.

sentences.text: despite having knowledge that they were no longer the lawful owners of the said land after executing the sale deed dated 03.05.2024, the accused persons, through forgery, conspiracy, and dishonest conduct, executed another sale deed in favour of Durjendra Kushwah, thereby causing wrongful loss to the complainant and unlawfully obtaining the sale consideration amount of Rs.6,85,000/-.

Therefore, the complainant requested that appropriate legal action be taken against the accused persons Suresh Jatav, Raju Kadam, Mahendra Kushwah, and Durjendra Kushwah for their acts of fraud, forgery, and criminal conspiracy.
On the basis of aforesaid allegation, the present FIR has been registered against the present applicant and co-accused persons.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely i m p l i c a t e d i n t h i s c a s e . L e a r n e d c o u n s e l f o r t h e N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .

GWL:10604 3 MCRC-13520-2026 applicant further submits that the investigation in the matter has already been completed and the charge-sheet (challan) has been filed before the learned Trial Court.

He also submitted that co-accused persons namely Dujendra Singh Kushwah and Raju Kadam have already been granted benefit of bail by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court in vide orders dated 10.03.2026 and 17.02.2026 passed in M.Cr.C. No.10137/2026 and 4890/2026 respectively.
Hence, the applicant seeks parity also.

The applicant was is a bonafide owner of the land and he did not sell the same plots to two persons but, the another plot which is alleged to have been sold secondly, bears different survey number and is also of different measurement.
It is further argued that once the alleged plot was sold by way of a registered sale deed, then it is not possible for the applicant to sell the same to some other person.
Learned counsel also contended that this FIR is a counterblast of the FIR registered by the present applicant against the complainant.
And just because, the complainant failed to get the land nominated his name, he has falsely implicated the present applicant.
The applicant is a permanent resident of District Guna and undertakes to cooperate with the investigation as well as the trial.
It is also submitted that there is no likelihood of the applicant absconding or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
On these grounds, it is prayed that this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.

Per contra, learned counsel for the State vehemently opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail and submits that the investigation in the matter is still pending and that the applicant has criminal antecedents of one criminal NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10604 4 MCRC-13520-2026 case.
Learned counsel for the complainant also vehemently opposes the present anticipatory bail application and prays for its rejection.
Heard the counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

From perusal of the record, this court finds that earlier the applicant was given notice under Section 41(a) of the Cr.P.C. but, at the relevant point of time, he did remain absent and did not make himself available before the prosecution/trial court.
This is a clear and willful disobedience/noncompliance.
Further, this Court finds that the present applicant had already surrendered the land in question for the purpose of road construction.
He along with his family members, had submitted a written application before the Tehsildar for surrender of the said land.
